(This Evening through Tuesday)... 
Issued at 238 PM EDT Tue Oct 13 2026

After another hot afternoon...a frontal boundary will move into the 
area from the north tonight and Wednesday with the potential for 
rain and scattered thunderstorms. Chances for thunderstorms will 
continue through Thursday night prior to a strong cold front passing 
through the area. Much cooler air will expand across the region 
Friday into the weekend with temperatures recovering to near normal 
levels by early next week.

Rest of This Afternoon through Thursday Night

Another very warm and breezy day for central Indiana as most of the 
earlier mid level clouds have moved off to the east. 18Z 
temperatures were in the 80s with the warmest readings again across 
the lower Wabash Valley in the upper 80s. KIND broke their daily 
record high shortly after 18Z as well.

Temperatures will climb a few more degrees through late afternoon 
with mostly sunny skies and breezy southwest winds continuing. There 
remains a strong likelihood of 90 degrees being reached at a number 
of locations across the southwest half of the forecast area. 

A frontal boundary across the Great Lakes this afternoon will 
slowly drift southeast into northern Indiana tonight as it remains 
nearly parallel to the mean flow aloft. Progressively deeper 
moisture associated with Hurricane Simon currently off the Mexican 
Pacific coast will advect northeast into the central Plains and then 
pool along the boundary into the region. This will serve as a 
catalyst to convective development late tonight as a westerly low 
level jet aligns along the boundary across the lower Great Lakes 
with additional convection developing initially over Kansas this 
evening growing upscale into an expansive convective cluster that 
will press into the mid Mississippi Valley by daybreak Wednesday.
The bulk of the storms that develop along the boundary late tonight 
will remain to the north of the forecast area until the predawn 
hours at the earliest

The convective cluster to our west will track east into the Wabash 
Valley Wednesday morning with showers and storms increasing in 
coverage into the afternoon as the boundary slides into the forecast 
area and rich plume of tropical moisture sidling along it expands 
into the region. PWATS will rise to near 2 inches Wednesday 
afternoon focused across the southern half of the forecast area with 
modest elevated instability supporting a few stronger cells that 
will continue into the evening as the boundary settles near or just 
north of the Ohio River. Showers may linger in vicinity of the 
boundary Wednesday night but high pressure passing to the north 
across the Great Lakes will advect drier mid level air into the 
forecast area. This will limit rainfall coverage but the presence of 
a sharp inversion near 850mb will trap low level moisture and clouds 
most if not all of the night.

The front will pull back north Thursday in response to a surface low 
ejecting out of the central Plains in tandem with jet phasing aloft. 
There remains potential for a few stronger storms...especially ahead 
of a strong cold front that will sweep across the area late Thursday 
afternoon and evening with damaging winds as the most likely threat. 
Behind the frontal passage Thursday night...much cooler air will 
advect into the area  1 to 2 inches of rain is possible focused 
especially across the northern half of the forecast area by Thursday 
evening with winds becoming gusty as well as cold advection 
establishes in the post-frontal environment.

Temps...Clouds and periodic showers and storms will keep temps 
ranging from the mid 70s north to the lower 80s south on Wednesday 
with a muggy airmass. Thursday highs will range from the 70s into 
the lower 80s in the lower Wabash Valley ahead of the cold front 
before much cooler air arrives for Friday and Saturday. Lows tonight 
will largely remain near 70 with low to mid 60s for most of the 
region Wednesday night. In the wake of the Thursday night frontal 
passage...lows will fall into the low and mid 50s.

Friday Through Tuesday

In the wake of the frontal passage early Friday...the upper trough 
will settle and amplify across much of the eastern half of the 
country into the first part of the weekend before shifting east by 
Sunday. The coolest air of the Fall so far will advect into the area 
Friday and Saturday. Intense cold advection combined with a sharp 
pressure gradient behind the front will likely bring strong wind 
gusts peaking at 35 to 40 mph throughout the day Friday along with 
diurnal cu and perhaps a few light showers across the northeast half 
of the forecast area. Winds will relax Friday night into Saturday as 
a 1035mb surface high moves across the area. Return flow will 
develop as early as Sunday with the high moving east into the Mid 
Atlantic region. Deep subsidence supports an extended period of 
mainly clear skies Saturday into early next week.
